IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p141/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p141/r4.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p141/r4.claim: An oath may omit its answer when later words make it clear; here the implied answer is that the dead will be resurrected, which the disbelievers deny.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p141/r4.anchor: ومن الاختصار: القسم بلا جواب إذا كان في الكلام بعده ما يدل على الجواب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p526#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p526#2/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p526#2/r4.claim: حَادَ عن الشيء means to turn away or incline from it; he gives the verbal nouns حيودا، حيدة، and حيدودة.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p526#2/r4.anchor: حاد عن الشيء: مال عنه، حيودا وحيدة وحيدودة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p529/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p529/r3.speaker: الأعرج وشيبة وأبو جعفر وابن وثاب والأعمش وابن عتبة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p529/r3.claim: These readers pronounce إذا with one hamza as a declarative form; it may conceal an interrogative hamza or state their claim that they will return after becoming dust.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p529/r3.anchor: وقرأ الأعرج، وشيبة، وأبو جعفر، وابن وثاب، والأعمش، وابن عتبة عن ابن عامر: إذا بهمزة واحدة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p529/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p529/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p529/r4.claim: With the interrogative reading, the time expression depends on an omitted verb meaning 'Will we be raised when we die?'; 'that' points to resurrection, which they deem remote.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p529/r4.anchor: فالظرف منصوب بمضمر، أي: أنبعث إذا متنا؟ وإليه الإشارة بقوله ذلك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p529/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p529/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p529/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī allows رجع to mean 'the returned thing' and to be God's own expression of their rejection; Abū Ḥayyān calls this interpretation astonishing and unintelligible to Arabs.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p529/r5.anchor: وكون ذلك رجع بعيد بمعنى مرجوع، وأنه من كلام الله تعالى

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p434/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p434/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p434/r1.claim: The Qur’an’s grandeur proves its divine origin; calling it poetry or soothsaying is a pretext for denying resurrection, driven by pride and confusion, although God knows what earth consumes and records people’s deeds and words.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p434/r1.anchor: The grandeur and magnificence of the Qur’ ān bear witness that it is the word of God

NAHHAS:v4p219/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p219/r10.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p219/r10.claim: The objection asks whether they will be resurrected after dying and becoming dust; al-Farra says baʿīd here means it will not happen, a recognized Arabic usage.
NAHHAS:v4p219/r10.anchor: أي أنبعث إذا متنا ( وكنا ترابا ذلك رجع بعيد ) ومعنى بعيد عند الفراء

SAMIN-DURR:50:3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:50:3/r1.speaker: العامة
SAMIN-DURR:50:3/r1.claim: The common reading has two hamzas and is interrogative. Ibn ʿĀmir in one transmission, Abū Jaʿfar, al-Aʿmash, and al-Aʿraj use one hamza, possibly interrogative with the particle omitted or declarative.
SAMIN-DURR:50:3/r1.anchor: قرأ العامة بالاستفهام، وابن عامر في رواية، وأبو جعفر والأعمش والأعرج بهمزة واحدة، فتحتمل الاستفهام كالجمهور، وإنما حذف الأداة للدلالة، وتحتمل الإخبار بذلك.

SAMIN-DURR:50:3/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:50:3/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:50:3/r2.claim: In the common interrogative reading, an implicit verb such as أنبعث or أنرجع governs إذا.
SAMIN-DURR:50:3/r2.anchor: والناصب للظرف في قراءة الجمهور مقدر أي: أنبعث أو أنرجع إذا متنا.

SAMIN-DURR:50:3/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:50:3/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:50:3/r3.claim: With the declarative reading, the answer after إذا is omitted: “we returned.”
SAMIN-DURR:50:3/r3.anchor: وجواب " إذا " على قراءة الخبر محذوف أي: رجعنا.

SAMIN-DURR:50:3/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:50:3/r4.speaker: قيل
SAMIN-DURR:50:3/r4.claim: Some take ذلك رجع as the answer to إذا with the fāʾ deleted; the majority disallow this except in poetry.
SAMIN-DURR:50:3/r4.anchor: وقيل: قوله: " ذلك رجع " على حذف الفاء، وهذا رأي بعضهم. والجمهور لا يجوز ذلك إلا في شعر.

SAMIN-DURR:50:3/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:50:3/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:50:3/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī reads الرجع as “the thing returned” (resurrection), a divine answer exposing the deniers’ rejection; on this parse, stop before it.
SAMIN-DURR:50:3/r5.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون الرجع بمعنى المرجوع هو الجواب، ويكون من كلام الله تعالى، استبعادا لإنكارهم ما أنذروا به من البعث.

SAMIN-DURR:50:3/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:50:3/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:50:3/r6.claim: On al-Zamakhsharī’s parse, the adverb is governed by what “the warned” implies, namely the warning about resurrection.
SAMIN-DURR:50:3/r6.anchor: قلت: ما دل عليه المنذر من المنذر به وهو البعث

SAMIN-DURR:50:3/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:50:3/r7.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:50:3/r7.claim: The Shaykh sharply criticizes al-Zamakhsharī for understanding the passage this way.
SAMIN-DURR:50:3/r7.anchor: وأنحى عليه الشيخ في فهمه هذا الفهم.

ZAJJAJ:v5p41/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p41/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p41/r7.claim: The question means “shall we be raised when we have died and become dust?”; idhā must connect to a verb for the statement to have a point.
ZAJJAJ:v5p41/r7.anchor: أي أنبعث إذا - متنا وكنا ترابا. ولو لم يكن إذا متعلق لم يكن في الكلام فائدة.

ZAJJAJ:v5p42/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p42/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p42/r1.claim: The deniers call resurrection a remote return because they consider it far-fetched after death.
ZAJJAJ:v5p42/r1.anchor: أي يبعد عندنا أن نبعث بعد الموت.

ASAD-NOTES:50:1/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:50:1/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:50:1/r1.claim: The deniers find resurrection strange and ask how they could return after dying and becoming dust.
ASAD-NOTES:50:1/r1.anchor: after we have died and become mere dust? Such a return seems far-fetched indeed

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p437/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p437/r5.speaker: these disbelievers
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p437/r5.claim: They found it strange that a warner from among themselves had come and said resurrection after death and becoming dust was very improbable.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p437/r5.anchor: these disbelievers had said: “It is a very strange thing

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p438/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p438/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p438/r2.claim: Their underlying resistance is that a person from their own community warns them of resurrection; accepting him as God’s messenger weighs heavily on them, so they call the return improbable.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p438/r2.anchor: the real reason for their evasion is not what they are expressing but it is that they are surprised at the fact that a person from amongst themselves is warning them

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p438/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p438/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p438/r3.claim: Arrogance is the true cause: unwilling to accept one of their own as God’s messenger, they reject the Qur’an and deem the Hereafter unlikely; without arrogance they could recognize revelation and its arguments.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p438/r3.anchor: the real reason of their evasion is their arrogance: they are not ready to accept someone among them as a messenger of God

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p438/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p438/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p438/r6.claim: In this group’s context, the discourse addresses objections about death and resurrection that opponents use as excuses to oppose the Prophet.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p438/r6.anchor: those objections are dealt with which they would raise on death and on the possibility of resurrection.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p440/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p440/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p440/r1.claim: The rejecters deny a reality that is as evident as the midday sun.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p440/r1.anchor: they are denying a reality which is shinning over their heads like the midday sun.

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p281/r7.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p281/r7.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p281/r7.claim: Yahya, al-Aʿraj, Shayba, Abu Jaʿfar, and Safwan ibn ʿAmr read "إذا متنا" without an interrogative hamza.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p281/r7.anchor: قراءة يحيى والأعرج وشيبة وأبي جعفر وصفوان بن عمرو

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p281/r8.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p281/r8.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p281/r8.claim: One explanation supplies a deleted interrogative hamza from the common reading, but Ibn Jinnī recalls having judged this deletion explanation weak.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p281/r8.anchor: حذف همزة الاستفهام على القراءة العامة، فحذفها تخفيفا، وقد مضى نحو هذا، وذكرنا ضعفه

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p281/r9.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p281/r9.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p281/r9.claim: Alternatively, the reading is non-interrogative: after death and becoming dust, they would be brought back; "distant return" means implausible to them, not far off in time, since they denied resurrection altogether.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p281/r9.anchor: أن يكون غير مريد للهمزة، فكأنه قال: إذا متنا وكنا ترابا بعد رجعنا ونشورنا

QIRAAT-ER:50:3:2#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:50:3:2#1/r1.speaker: vw
QIRAAT-ER:50:3:2#1/r1.claim: The vw reading shifts mīm from kasra to ḍamma: mutnā follows the u-stem māta/yamūtu pattern, standard in Ḥijāz, while mitnā follows the alternative a-stem pattern.
QIRAAT-ER:50:3:2#1/r1.anchor: Form I māta has two conjugation patterns — māta/yamūtu with u-stem and māta/yamātu with a-stem

ALUSI-FULL:v26p172#4/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p172#4/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p172#4/r1.claim: The opening reports their astonishment, intensifies their denial, or identifies the point they find astonishing.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p172#4/r1.anchor: تقرير للتعجب وتأكيد للأنكار أو بيان لموضع تعجبهم

ALUSI-FULL:v26p172#4/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p172#4/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p172#4/r2.claim: The governing word for إذا is omitted but obvious: when we die and become dust, will we return, despite the change from life to death?
ALUSI-FULL:v26p172#4/r2.anchor: والعامل في ( إذا ) مضمر غني عن البيان لغاية شهرته

ALUSI-FULL:v26p172#4/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p172#4/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p172#4/r3.claim: ذلك points to the disputed return, resurrection after death.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p172#4/r3.anchor: إشارة إلى محل النزاع وهو الرجع والبعث بعد الموت

ALUSI-FULL:v26p172#4/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p172#4/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p172#4/r4.claim: They call the return remote from imagination, ordinary experience, or possibility.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p172#4/r4.anchor: أي عن الأوهام أو العادة أو الأمكان

ALUSI-FULL:v26p172#4/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p172#4/r5.speaker: غير مسمى
ALUSI-FULL:v26p172#4/r5.claim: An alternative takes رجع as a response or reply, as in “this is the reply to your letter”; ذلك then points back to their question.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p172#4/r5.anchor: الرجع بمعنى المرجوع أي الجواب يقال هذا رجع رسالتك

ALUSI-FULL:v26p172#4/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p172#4/r6.speaker: غير مسمى
ALUSI-FULL:v26p172#4/r6.claim: On the reply reading, the sentence is God's speech describing their answer to the warner as far-fetched; إذا is governed by the warned-of resurrection.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p172#4/r6.anchor: والجملة من كلام الله تعالى والمعنى ذلك جواب بعيد منهم لمنذرهم

ALUSI-FULL:v26p172#4/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p172#4/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p172#4/r7.claim: The objection that the reply reading leaves إذا without a governor fails: their answer itself shows they had been warned of resurrection.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p172#4/r7.anchor: فقد علم أنه أنذرهم بالبعث ليصلح ذلك جوابا له

ALUSI-FULL:v26p172#4/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p172#4/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p172#4/r8.claim: Al-Alusi considers رجع meaning “reply” remote; Abu Hayyan calls it a strange meaning beyond Arab comprehension.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p172#4/r8.anchor: هذا الوجه في نفسه بعيد بل قال أبو حيان : أنه مفهوم عجيب

ALUSI-FULL:v26p172#4/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p172#4/r9.speaker: الأعرج، شيبة، أبو جعفر، ابن وثاب، الأعمش، ابن عتبة عن ابن عامر
ALUSI-FULL:v26p172#4/r9.claim: These readers use one hamza in إذا, resembling an indicative form; it may be an interrogative with its hamza omitted or a declarative.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p172#4/r9.anchor: ابن عتبة عن ابن عامر ( إذا ) بهمزة واحدة على صورة الخبر

ALUSI-FULL:v26p172#4/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p172#4/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p172#4/r10.claim: If read declaratively, the answer is omitted: when we die and become dust, we shall return.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p172#4/r10.anchor: وأضمر جواب ( إذا ) أي إذا متنا وكنا ترابا رجعنا

ALUSI-FULL:v26p172#4/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p172#4/r11.speaker: صاحب اللوامح
ALUSI-FULL:v26p172#4/r11.claim: The author of al-Lawami permits ذلك رجع بعيد as the conditional answer after deletion of فاء; grammarians otherwise allow this only in poetic necessity.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p172#4/r11.anchor: وأجاز صاحب اللوامح أن يكون الجواب ذلك رجع بعيد

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p356/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p356/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p356/r4.claim: The question omits “will we be raised?” because context makes resurrection understood; they call return to life far-fetched and impossible.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p356/r4.anchor: ترك ذكر البعث لدلالة الكلام عليه

BAYDAWI-FULL:50:3-5/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:50:3-5/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:50:3-5/r1.claim: The implied question is whether they return after dying and becoming dust, as the following phrase shows.
BAYDAWI-FULL:50:3-5/r1.anchor: أي أنرجع إذا متنا وصرنا ترابا

BAYDAWI-FULL:50:3-5/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:50:3-5/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:50:3-5/r2.claim: The return seems remote from imagination, customary experience, or possibility; الرجع may instead mean the returned thing.
BAYDAWI-FULL:50:3-5/r2.anchor: بعيد عن الوهم أو العادة أو الإمكان

BIQAI-FULL:v7p246/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p246/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p246/r1.claim: Their denial does not stem from rejecting the Qurʾān's glory or the Prophet's truth; rather, the unbelievers are astonished.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p246/r1.anchor: { بل } أي أن تكذيبهم ليس لإنكار شيء من مجده ولا لإنكار صدقك الذي هو من مجده بل لأنهم { عجبوا }

BIQAI-FULL:v7p246/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p246/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p246/r6.claim: Their reasoning is inconsistent: they marvel at a human messenger and being returned from dust, yet accept stone gods and do not marvel that they first came to life from dust.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p246/r6.anchor: لأنهم عجبوا أن كان الرسول بشرا وأوجبوا أن يكون الإله حجرا , وعبجوا من أن يعادوا من تراب , وتثبت له الحياة

BIQAI-FULL:v7p246/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p246/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p246/r9.claim: The regular return of day and night, revival of dead land, first life in animals, and emergence of plants, trees, and fruit all make resurrection evident rather than strange.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p246/r9.anchor: وأما من جهة البعث فإن أكثر ما في الكون مثل ذلك من إعادة كل من الملوين بعد ذهابه وإحياء الأرض من بعد موتها

BIQAI-FULL:v7p246/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p246/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p246/r10.claim: Their objection imagines their souls separated from their bodies at death and their bodies reduced to dust indistinguishable from the earth's soil.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p246/r10.anchor: { إذا متنا } ففارقت أرواحنا أشباحنا { وكنا ترابا } لا فرق بينه وبين تراب الأرض

DURR-FULL:v7p589/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p589/r1.speaker: ابن جريج
DURR-FULL:v7p589/r1.claim: Ibn Jurayj says the deniers rejected resurrection, asking who could restore them to life.
DURR-FULL:v7p589/r1.anchor: عن ابن جريج في قوله {ذلك رجع بعيد} قال: أنكروا البعث فقالوا: من يستطيع أن يرجعنا ويحيينا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p279/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p279/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p279/r2.claim: This points to the situation in which the Prophet calls them to believe in resurrection, which the next verse spells out.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p279/r2.anchor: والإشارة بقولهم { هذا شيء عجيب } إلى ما هو جار في مقام مقالتهم تلك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p279/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p279/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p279/r3.claim: Their question expresses astonishment and rejection, meant to make listeners regard resurrection as impossible; they base their wonder on the timing after death and bodily decay.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p279/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p279/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p279/r4.claim: The questioned predicate is omitted after idhā: the implied question is whether they will return to life after death and reduction to dust, which they consider maximally inconceivable.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p279/r4.anchor: والمستفهم عنه محذوف دل عليه ظرف { أئذا متنا وكنا ترابا }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p279/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p279/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p279/r5.claim: The declarative statement repeats and confirms the question directly, after its meaning was conveyed indirectly by ellipsis; explicit confirmation is clearer.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p279/r5.anchor: وجملة { ذلك رجع بعيد } مؤكدة لجملة { أئذا متنا وكنا ترابا }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p279/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p279/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p279/r6.claim: Rujʿ is the verbal noun for returning to life; baʿīd means beyond rational conception, hence impossible.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p279/r6.anchor: والرجع : مصدر رجع ، أي الرجوع إلى الحياة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p156/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p156/r9.speaker: الأعرج وشيبة وأبو جعفر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p156/r9.claim: Al-Araj, Shayba, and Abu Jaafar read إذا declaratively, without the interrogative hamza; رجع بعيد is its predicate.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p156/r9.anchor: وقرأ الأعرج وشيبة وأبو جعفر «إذا» على الخبر دون استفهام، والعامل رجع بعيد،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p156/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p156/r10.speaker: ابن جني
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p156/r10.claim: Ibn Jinni allows the sense: when we die, are we then returned? ذلك رجع بعيد supplies the predicate and answer.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p156/r10.anchor: ذلك رجع بعيد على هذا الفعل الذي هو بعد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p156/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p156/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p156/r11.claim: Raj is the verbal noun of raja'tuhu, to return something.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p156/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p156/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p156/r12.claim: The alleged remoteness of resurrection is its supposed impossibility in people's minds and thoughts.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p156/r12.anchor: وقوله بعيد في الأوهام والفكر كونه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p156/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p156/r13.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p156/r13.claim: God knows what the earth consumes of Adam's descendants and preserves it in a record, so their return is fully known.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p156/r13.anchor: ما تأكل الأرض من ابن آدم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p6#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p6#2/r1.speaker: الأخفش
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p6#2/r1.claim: Al-Akhfash reads the question as a response to an implied statement: “You will be returned,” followed by their objection about being dead and dust.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p6#2/r1.anchor: قال الأخفش هذا الكلام على جواب كأنه قيل لهم إنكم ترجعون فقالوا أئذا متنا وكنا ترابا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p6#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p6#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p6#2/r2.claim: Another parse supplies an oath by Qaf and the Quran that they will be raised, followed by the question about being dead and dust.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p6#2/r2.anchor: وقال غيره تقدير الكلام ق والقرآن ليبعثن فقال أئذا متنا وكنا ترابا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p6#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p6#2/r3.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p6#2/r3.claim: Ibn Jarir links their astonishment at God's warning for denying Muhammad to their claim that resurrection is strange: they were told they would learn the outcome when raised.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p6#2/r3.anchor: وقال ابن جرير لما تعجبوا من وعيد الله على تكذيبهم بمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p6#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p6#2/r5.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p6#2/r5.claim: Ibn Qutayba says “far-fetched” means that it will not happen.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p6#2/r5.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة أي لا يكون

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p394#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p394#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p394#2/r6.claim: Ibn Kathir prefers the implicit answer in the ensuing message: establishing prophethood and resurrection; Qur'anic oaths often work this way, as in another sura.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p394#2/r6.anchor: بل الجواب هو مضمون الكلام بعد القسم، وهو إثبات النبوة، وإثبات المعاد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p394#2/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p394#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p394#2/r8.claim: They ask how they can return to their former bodily form after death, decay, severed limbs, and becoming dust; they regard resurrection as impossible.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p394#2/r8.anchor: وتقطعت الأوصال منا، وصرنا ترابا، كيف يمكن الرجوع بعد ذلك إلى هذه البنية والتركيب

BURSEVI:v9p82#3/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p82#3/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p82#3/r9.claim: They ask whether, after dying, their souls separate from bodies and they become indistinguishable from earth, they will be returned and raised despite the great difference from their former living state; the interrogative rejects resurrection.
BURSEVI:v9p82#3/r9.anchor: أي أحين نموت فتفارق أرواحنا أشباحنا ونصير ترابا لا فرق بيننا وبين تراب الأرض

JISHUMI:v9p6545/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6545/r3.speaker: أبي
JISHUMI:v9p6545/r3.claim: Ubayy reports that the Prophet said whoever recites Sūrat Qāf will have death's agonies eased; no grading is stated.
JISHUMI:v9p6545/r3.anchor: وعن أبي، عن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم -: من قرأ سورة (ق) هون الله عليه سكرات الموت

JISHUMI:v9p6545/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6545/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6545/r4.claim: Qāf opens with resurrection, the Qurʾān, and proofs of God's oneness, following al-Ḥujurāt's close on faith and its conditions.
JISHUMI:v9p6545/r4.anchor: ولما ختم سورة (الحجرات) بذكر الإيمان وشرائطه افتتح هذه السورة بما يجب الإيمان به من البعث والقرآن وأدلة التوحيد

JISHUMI:v9p6545/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6545/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6545/r8.claim: Marjiʿ is the verbal noun of rajaʿa, return.
JISHUMI:v9p6545/r8.anchor: والمرجع: مصدر رجع، وهو الرجوع، يقال: رجعته رجعا ورجع هو رجوعا.

JISHUMI:v9p6550/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6550/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6550/r1.claim: Rationally, resurrection concerns those entitled to reward or compensation; revelation says all living beings will be restored.
JISHUMI:v9p6550/r1.anchor: قلنا: في العقل من له حق الثواب أو عوض، والشرع ورد بإعادة جميع الأحياء.

JISHUMI:v9p6550/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6550/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6550/r2.claim: Resurrection is demonstrated by God's power over bodies and His knowledge of their parts.
JISHUMI:v9p6550/r2.anchor: قلنا: بكونه قادرا على الأجسام التي لا يقدر عليها غير القادر للذات، وبكونه عالما بالأجزاء

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p383#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p383#2/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p383#2/r5.claim: Their denial of resurrection is especially absurd: they acknowledge God’s power to originate all things, admit the first creation, and reason requires recompense.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p383#2/r5.anchor: مع علمهم بقدرة الله تعالى على خلق السماوات والأرض وما بينهما

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p383#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p383#2/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p383#2/r6.claim: He replaces the pronoun with disbelievers to mark the gravity of their unbelief, focusing on their rejection of resurrection.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p383#2/r6.anchor: وضع الكافرون موضع الضمير للشهادة على أنهم في قولهم هذا مقدمون

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p383#2/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p383#2/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p383#2/r7.claim: That points to the return to life after death.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p383#2/r7.anchor: إشارة إلى الرجع ؛ وإذا منصوب بمضمر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p383#2/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p383#2/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p383#2/r8.claim: The time adverb is governed by an implied verb: will we be returned when we have died and decayed?

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p383#2/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p383#2/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p383#2/r9.claim: Far means beyond customary experience and what the mind considers plausible.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p383#2/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p383#2/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p383#2/r10.claim: Alternatively rajʿ means the returned answer, making this God’s comment that their denial of resurrection is itself outlandish.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p383#2/r10.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون الرجع بمعنى المرجوع . وهو الجواب

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p383#2/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p383#2/r11.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p383#2/r11.claim: A reading has idhā in declarative form rather than a question; it is understood as when we die after we have returned, as the following phrase indicates.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p383#2/r11.anchor: وقرىء : ( إذا متنا ) على لفظ الخبر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p383#2/r12.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p383#2/r12.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p383#2/r12.claim: If rajʿ means the returned answer, the time adverb is governed by the resurrection matter implied by the word warner.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p383#2/r12.anchor: ما دل عليه المنذر من المنذر به ، وهو البعث

MUQATIL:50:3/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:50:3/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:50:3/r1.claim: The deniers say that returning to life after death and becoming dust is far-fetched, denying that resurrection will happen.
MUQATIL:50:3/r1.anchor: إلى الحياة { بعيد } [آية: 3] بأن البعث غير كائن

MUQATIL:50:3/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:50:3/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:50:3/r2.claim: The verse was revealed about Quraysh deniers Abu ibn Khalaf, Abu al-Ashaddayn (Usayda ibn Kalda), and the brothers Nabh and Munabbih, sons of al-Hajjaj; they asked how God could revive them once they were dust scattered in the earth.
MUQATIL:50:3/r2.anchor: نزلت في أبي بن خلف الجمحي، وأبي الأشدين واسمه أسيدة بن كلدة، وهما من بني جمح

NASAFI-FULL:v4p170/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p170/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p170/r1.claim: Their question expresses astonishment and intensifies the claim that resurrection is unlikely and deserves denial.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p170/r1.anchor: دلالة على تعجبهم من البعث ادخل في الاستبعاد واحق بالانكار

NASAFI-FULL:v4p170/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p170/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p170/r2.claim: Calling them the disbelievers instead of using a pronoun marks the gravity of the unbelief in their statement.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p170/r2.anchor: ووضع الكافرون موضع الضمير للشهادة على انهم في قولهم هذا مقدمون على الكفر العظيم

NASAFI-FULL:v4p170/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p170/r4.speaker: نافع وعلى وحمزة وحفص
NASAFI-FULL:v4p170/r4.claim: Nāfiʿ, ʿAlī, Ḥamza, and Ḥafṣ read mitnā with the vowel form recorded in the commentary.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p170/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p170/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p170/r5.claim: Baʿīd means judged far-fetched and rejected, remote from imagination and ordinary experience, as in saying this is a distant statement.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p170/r5.anchor: مستبعد مسنكر كفولك هذا قول بعيد اى بعيد من الوهم والعادة

NASAFI-FULL:v4p170/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p170/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p170/r6.claim: Alternatively, al-rajʿ means return or response and the words are God's characterization of their denial of the promised resurrection; on this reading a pause after turāban is good, with the time adverb governed by the warning of resurrection.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p170/r6.anchor: ويجوز ان يكون الرجع بمعنى الرجوع وهو الجواب ويكون من كلام الله تعالى استبعاد الانكار

QURTUBI-FULL:50:1-4/r21.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:50:1-4/r21.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:50:1-4/r21.claim: The disbelievers' question has an omitted predicate: will we be raised after dying and becoming dust?
QURTUBI-FULL:50:1-4/r21.anchor: { أإذا متنا وكنا ترابا } نبعث ففيه إضمار.

QURTUBI-FULL:50:1-4/r22.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:50:1-4/r22.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:50:1-4/r22.claim: Rajaʿ means return; they call resurrection a remote return, meaning impossible.
QURTUBI-FULL:50:1-4/r22.anchor: الرجع الرد أي هو رد بعيد أي محال.

QURTUBI-FULL:50:1-4/r23.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:50:1-4/r23.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:50:1-4/r23.claim: A second ellipsis supplies their repeated objection: they said, “Will we be resurrected when we die?”
QURTUBI-FULL:50:1-4/r23.anchor: وفيه إضمار آخر أي وقالوا أنبعث إذا متنا.

QURTUBI-FULL:50:1-4/r24.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:50:1-4/r24.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:50:1-4/r24.claim: Resurrection need not have been mentioned immediately before: it occurs elsewhere, the Qur'an is like one surah, and a warner's warning entails afterlife punishment and judgment.
QURTUBI-FULL:50:1-4/r24.anchor: وذكر البعث وإن لم يجر هاهنا فقد جرى في مواضع، والقرآن كالسورة الواحدة.

RAZI-FULL:v28p125/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p125/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p125/r1.claim: Rāzī says Sūrat Qāf is recited in Eid prayer: Eid's festivity should remind worshippers of the gathering for judgment and deter heedlessness and sin; the sūra's Quranic reminder suits the day.
RAZI-FULL:v28p125/r1.anchor: الأول : أن هذه السورة تقرأ في صلاة العيد ، لقوله تعالى فيها { ذلك يوم الخروج } ( ق : 42 )

RAZI-FULL:v28p125/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p125/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p125/r2.claim: Sūrat Qāf and Sūrat Ṣād share openings with an isolated letter, an oath by the Quran, “bal,” and an expression of wonder; each also opens and closes with a reminder about the Quran.
RAZI-FULL:v28p125/r2.anchor: الثاني : هذه السورة ، وسورة { ص } تشتركان في افتتاح أولهما بالحروف المعجم والقسم بالقرآن وقوله { بل } والتعجب

RAZI-FULL:v28p125/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p125/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p125/r3.claim: Ṣād foregrounds the first principle, God's unity, while Qāf foregrounds resurrection; Ṣād ends by recalling Adam's creation as proof of unity, and Qāf ends with the gathering.
RAZI-FULL:v28p125/r3.anchor: والثالث : وهو أن في تلك السورة صرف العناية إلى تقرير الأصل الأول وهو التوحيد ، بقوله تعالى : { أجعل الالهة إلاها واحدا }

RAZI-FULL:v28p130#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p130#2/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
RAZI-FULL:v28p130#2/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says “this is a strange thing” is a second expression of wonder, about resurrection and the warner's warning of it.
RAZI-FULL:v28p130#2/r1.anchor: قال الزمخشري هذا تعجب آخر من أمر آخر وهو الحشر الذي أشار إليه

RAZI-FULL:v28p130#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p130#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p130#2/r3.claim: In Ṣād, “indeed this is astonishing” follows the challenge to make one God, whereas in Qāf the phrase follows the warner's arrival and precedes the separate objection to resurrection.
RAZI-FULL:v28p130#2/r3.anchor: هو أن هناك ذكر { إن هاذا لشىء عجاب } بعد الاستفهام الإنكاري فقال : { أجعل الالهة إلاها واحدا إن هاذا لشىء عجاب }

RAZI-FULL:v28p130#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p130#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p130#2/r4.claim: “That return is far” already expresses wonder at resurrection, so assigning “this is strange” to resurrection would repeat it; instead it confirms their wonder at the messenger after God rebukes misplaced amazement.
RAZI-FULL:v28p130#2/r4.anchor: الثاني : ههنا وجد بعد الاستبعاد بالاستفهام أمر يؤدي معنى التعجب وهو قولهم { ذلك رجع بعيد } فإنه استبعاد وهو كالتعجب

RAZI-FULL:v28p130#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p130#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p130#2/r6.claim: Rāzī also distinguishes the near “this” from the distant “that”: the first points to the present arrival of the warner, the second to the future return.
RAZI-FULL:v28p130#2/r6.anchor: ويدل عليه أيضا قوله تعالى : { ذلك رجع بعيد } ( ق: 3 ) بلفظ الإشارة إلى البعد ، وقوله هذا إشارة إلى الحاضر القريب

RAZI-FULL:v28p131#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p131#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p131#2/r1.claim: Rāzī links the opponents' astonishment at the messenger to their dismissal of his message, citing their accusations that he would turn people from ancestral worship and that his message was fabricated.
RAZI-FULL:v28p131#2/r1.anchor: وهذا كما قال تعالى عنهم { قالوا ما هاذا إلا رجل يريد أن يصدكم عما كان يعبد ءاباؤكم }

RAZI-FULL:v28p131#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p131#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p131#2/r2.claim: Their question is an explicit or implied denial prompted by the warner: warning of lasting punishment entails resurrection.
RAZI-FULL:v28p131#2/r2.anchor: لأن الإنذار لما لم يكن إلا بالعذاب المقيم والعقاب الأليم ، كان فيه الإشارة للحشر

RAZI-FULL:v28p131#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p131#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p131#2/r3.claim: “That” points to the warned-of return, while “this is strange” points to the messenger's arrival; the messenger is present but the warned-of event is distant.
RAZI-FULL:v28p131#2/r3.anchor: ذلك إشارة إلى ما قاله وهو الإنذار ، وقوله { هاذا شىء عجيب } ( ق: 2 ) إشارة إلى المجيء على ما قلنا

RAZI-FULL:v28p131#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p131#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p131#2/r4.claim: Rāzī explains rajʿ as a verbal noun usable with a transitive sense; rujuʿ and al-rujʿā are intransitive verbal nouns, and rajʿ can also be intransitive.
RAZI-FULL:v28p131#2/r4.anchor: والرجوع مصدره إذا كان لازما ، وكذلك الرجعى مصدر عند لزومه

RAZI-FULL:v28p131#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p131#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p131#2/r5.claim: The phrase can mean a far-off return, supported by 96:8, or a far-off raising, supported by 79:10; on the transitive reading they deny that resurrection is possible.
RAZI-FULL:v28p131#2/r5.anchor: فإن قلنا هو من المتعدي ، فقد أنكروا كونه مقدورا في نفسه

STUDYQURAN:50:3/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:50:3/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:50:3/r1.claim: Disbelievers say this to disparage the Quran’s teaching of bodily resurrection.
STUDYQURAN:50:3/r1.anchor: These are the words of the disbelievers when they disparage the Quranic teaching regarding bodily resurrection

QUSHAYRI:v3p225/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p225/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p225/r3.claim: One proposed, omitted response to the oath is that they will indeed be raised at the Resurrection.
QUSHAYRI:v3p225/r3.anchor: وجواب القسم محذوف ومعناه لتبعثن في القيامة

QUSHAYRI:v3p225/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p225/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p225/r8.claim: The unbelievers deny resurrection and deem it far-fetched that they could be raised after dying and becoming dust.
QUSHAYRI:v3p225/r8.anchor: وقد مضى القول في إنكارهم للبعث واستبعادهم ذلك

TABATABAI:50:1-4/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:50:1-4/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:50:1-4/r1.claim: The sūrah warns of Resurrection and explains the polytheists' astonishment: death reduces identity to dust without trace, so they wonder how people return; God's encompassing knowledge and Preserved Book answer them, and past nations' destruction warns them.
TABATABAI:50:1-4/r1.anchor: تذكر الدعوة وتشير إلى ما فيها من الإنذار بالمعاد وجحد المشركين به واستعجابهم ذلك

TABATABAI:50:1-4/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:50:1-4/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:50:1-4/r4.claim: Resurrection is the sūrah's focus; the author highlights the unveiling at 50:22, Hell's response at 50:30, and the Garden's abundance at 50:35.
TABATABAI:50:1-4/r4.anchor: وبالجملة مصب الكلام في السورة هو المعاد

TABATABAI:50:1-4/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:50:1-4/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:50:1-4/r5.claim: The sūrah is Meccan by its context; claims that the verse or verses about creation of heavens and earth are exceptions have no textual evidence.

TABATABAI:50:1-4/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:50:1-4/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:50:1-4/r6.claim: The opening briefly signals the Resurrection, disbelievers' incredulity, the response, and threat; later the sūrah details the answer and threat.
TABATABAI:50:1-4/r6.anchor: ثم الإشارة إلى تفصيل الجواب والتهديد ثانيا

TABATABAI:50:1-4/r14.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:50:1-4/r14.speaker: author
TABATABAI:50:1-4/r14.claim: ‘Rather’ diverts from the omitted oath response: either they marvel that a warner came from among them, or they marvel at the true Resurrection they were warned of.
TABATABAI:50:1-4/r14.anchor: إضراب عن مضمون جواب القسم المحذوف فكأنه قيل

TABATABAI:50:2-4/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:50:2-4/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:50:2-4/r5.claim: “Return” and “returning” are synonymous here; “distant” means contrary to reason.
TABATABAI:50:2-4/r5.anchor: الرجع والرجوع بمعنى والمراد بالبعد البعد عن العقل

TABATABAI:50:2-4/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:50:2-4/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:50:2-4/r6.claim: The response to “when we die and become dust?” is omitted and supplied from “that is a distant return”: “shall we be raised and returned?”
TABATABAI:50:2-4/r6.anchor: والتقدير ءإذا متنا وكنا ترابا نبعث ونرجع

TABATABAI:50:2-4/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:50:2-4/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:50:2-4/r7.claim: The omitted question marks their astonishment and suggests the claim is so incredible to them that it scarcely deserves stating.
TABATABAI:50:2-4/r7.anchor: وإنما حذف للإشارة إلى أنه عجيب بحيث لا ينبغي أن يذكر

TABATABAI:50:2-4/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:50:2-4/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:50:2-4/r8.claim: Their objection parallels the denial in 32:10 that people will be created anew after being lost in the earth.
TABATABAI:50:2-4/r8.anchor: والآية في مساق قوله وقالوا ءإذا ضللنا في الأرض ءإنا لفي خلق جديد السجدة 10

AKHFASH:v2p522/r2.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p522/r2.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p522/r2.claim: The phrase omits an explicit statement that resurrection is occurring because it answers an assertion that they will return: they object that return after becoming dust is remote.
AKHFASH:v2p522/r2.anchor: لم يذكر "انه رجع" وذلك - والله أعلم - لأنه كان على جواب كأنه قيل لهم: إنكم ترجعون

TABRISI:50:1-5/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:50:1-5/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:50:1-5/r9.claim: The governing verb for “when we die” is implicit: the intended question is whether they will be resurrected after death.
TABRISI:50:1-5/r9.anchor: والعامل في أإذا متنا مضمر والتقدير أإذا متنا بعثنا

TABRISI:50:1-5/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:50:1-5/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:50:1-5/r15.claim: The disbelievers called Muhammad's message astonishing because they denied both a messenger from their own people and resurrection after death.
TABRISI:50:1-5/r15.anchor: فأنكروا رسالته وانكروا البعث بعد الموت

TABRISI:50:1-5/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:50:1-5/r16.speaker: author
TABRISI:50:1-5/r16.claim: They deem return to life far beyond imagination and impossible, so they deny that it can occur.
TABRISI:50:1-5/r16.anchor: أي رد بعيد عن الأوهام وإعادة بعيدة عن الكون

FARRA:v3p75/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p75/r4.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p75/r4.claim: The question’s lead-in is omitted: the oath implies You will surely be raised after death; the disbelievers reject this and call resurrection a far-fetched return.
FARRA:v3p75/r4.anchor: وقوله إذا متنا وكنا ترابا (3) . كلام لم يظهر قبله ما يكون هذا جوابا له، ولكن معناه مضمر

FARRA:v3p75/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p75/r5.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p75/r5.claim: They deny resurrection outright; بعيد can describe someone far from the truth, as when a person errs in an answer.
FARRA:v3p75/r5.anchor: ثم قالوا : (ذلك رجع بعيد) (3) . جحدوه أصلا [و] قوله: (بعيد) كما تقول للرجل يخطىء في المسألة

THALABI:v9p93/r14.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p93/r14.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p93/r14.claim: The question means, “Will we be raised after we die and become dust?” The mention of resurrection is elided because the context makes it clear.
THALABI:v9p93/r14.anchor: أإذا متنا وكنا ترابا نبعث، فترك ذكر البعث لدلالة الكلام عليه.

THALABI:v9p93/r15.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p93/r15.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p93/r15.claim: They call resurrection a far-fetched return; the commentary gives the verb's forms as rajʿan and rujuʿan and cites its Quranic usage.
THALABI:v9p93/r15.anchor: ذلك رجع بعيد يقال: رجعته رجعا، فرجع هو رجوعا،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p377/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p377/r4.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p377/r4.claim: Al-Farra says the response is omitted and indicated by the question at 50:3: the oath means they will surely be resurrected, which they deny; al-Zajjaj also chooses this reading.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p377/r4.anchor: وقال الفراء: جواب القسم محذوف يدل عليه قوله: {أإذا متنا}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p379#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p379#2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p379#2/r1.claim: Al-Wahidi explains rajʿ as a return or reversal, citing the verb in 9:83.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p379#2/r1.anchor: الرجع معناه الرد. قال الله تعالى: {فإن رجعك الله إلى طائفة منهم}

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p417#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p417#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p417#2/r1.claim: The deniers mean that resurrection after death will not happen.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p417#2/r1.anchor: يريدون: البعث بعد الموت؛ أي لا يكون

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:50:1-4/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:50:1-4/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:50:1-4/r5.claim: Their question about being raised after death and becoming dust is an interrogative denial with an omitted answer.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:50:1-4/r5.anchor: أإذا متنا وكنا ترابا } نبعث؟ وهذا استفهام إنكار، وجوابه محذوف

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:50:1-4/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:50:1-4/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:50:1-4/r6.claim: They then outright deny resurrection, calling it an impossible return.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:50:1-4/r6.anchor: ذلك } أي: البعث { رجع بعيد } رد لا يكون. قال الله تعالى:

ELMALILI:50:1-5#3/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:50:1-5#3/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:50:1-5#3/r4.claim: On one reading, the next clause explains their amazement and makes their disbelief explicit: the particle fa is explanatory and “this” points to the Prophet’s warning.
ELMALILI:50:1-5#3/r4.anchor: Birisi taaccüblerini tefsir ve taaccüb noktasını tafsil ile küfürlerini tasrihtir. Bu surette فا tefsir, هذا Peygamber’in inzârına işarettir.

ELMALILI:50:1-5#3/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:50:1-5#3/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:50:1-5#3/r5.claim: On the other reading, after marveling at the Prophet’s mission they also marvel at resurrection: fa coordinates the clauses, and “this” refers ambiguously to their question about being raised after death.
ELMALILI:50:1-5#3/r5.anchor: İkincisi Peygamber’in bi‘setine taaccübden sonra âhirette ba‘se taaccüblerini beyandır. Bu surette فا atıf هذا mübhem olarak şu söze işaret olur

ELMALILI:50:1-5#3/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:50:1-5#3/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:50:1-5#3/r6.claim: The phrase calls resurrection after death a distant return, remote from reason or custom; “ircāʿ” can also mean a reply or response.
ELMALILI:50:1-5#3/r6.anchor: ba‘îd bir ircâ‘akıldan veya âdetten uzak olan bir iade, bir döndürüş yahut bir cevaptır.

MAJAZ:v2p222/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p222/r2.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p222/r2.claim: The phrase means a far-fetched return or restoration.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:50:1/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:50:1/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:50:1/r1.claim: The passage addresses monotheism, prophethood, and the afterlife; against denials of resurrection it directs people to God's knowledge and power, the first creation, and the blessings around them.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:50:1/r1.anchor: Hz. Peygamber’in Kur’an (vahiy) yoluyla alıp tebliğ ettiği inanç esasları içinde en önemlileri; bir tek Allah’a kulluk (tevhid), peygamberliğe iman (nübüvvet), öldükten sonra dirilmeye

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:50:1/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:50:1/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:50:1/r2.claim: The resurrection argument is that the God who brought all things from nothing can recreate them, and that He knows exactly what remains or decays in a body, so restoring its like and returning its soul is easy for Him.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:50:1/r2.anchor: Kur’an’ın bu şüpheye karşı ileri sürdüğü delilin iki önemli unsuru vardır

BURHAN:v3p333/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p333/r4.speaker: ابن الزبير
BURHAN:v3p333/r4.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr treats Qaf's move from denial of resurrection to visible signs in the sky and revived land as a comparable shift; these undeniable signs lead to the conclusion that resurrection will likewise occur.
BURHAN:v3p333/r4.anchor: وألحق به الأستاذ أبو جعفر بن الزبير

BURHAN:v3p333/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p333/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p333/r5.claim: After leaving the disbelievers' challenge unanswered and describing the heavens and rain as observable facts they could not deny, God concludes: “Thus is the emergence.”
BURHAN:v3p333/r5.anchor: وذكر اختلافهم المسبب عن تكذيبهم في قوله

DAMGHANI:v1p86/r2.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p86/r2.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p86/r2.claim: تراب in the question about being raised again means decayed remains.
DAMGHANI:v1p86/r2.anchor: فوجه منها : التراب بمعنى الرميم . قوله تعالى في سورة الرعد

BURHAN:v3p81/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p81/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p81/r7.claim: من is added after negation or its equivalent for emphasis, as in verses about a falling leaf, creation, and God's having a child or partner.
BURHAN:v3p81/r7.anchor: وأما من فإنها تزاد في الكلام الوارد بعد نفي أو شبهه نحو
